segs.text: Your crypto isn't inside your wallet.
parts: Your crypto isn't inside your wallet.

segs.text: A crypto wallet is more like a keyring. The coins live on the blockchain. The wallet holds the keys that prove they're yours.
parts: A crypto wallet is more like a keyring.
The coins live on the blockchain. The wallet holds the keys that prove they're yours.

segs.text: There are two keys. Your public address is like your UPI ID: share it, and people can pay you.
parts: There are two keys. Your public address is like your UPI ID:
share it, and people can pay you.

segs.text: Your private key is like your PIN and your signature combined. It approves every payment.
parts: Your private key is like your PIN and your signature combined.

segs.text: Most wallets turn that key into twelve or twenty-four simple words, called a recovery phrase.
parts: Most wallets turn that key into twelve or twenty-four simple words,

segs.text: Guessing a twenty-four word phrase means searching a number with seventy-eight digits. No computer today comes close.
parts: Guessing a twenty-four word phrase means searching a number with seventy-eight digits.

segs.text: The catch: there's no forgot-password button. Lose the words, and the funds are gone. Share them, and so are the funds.
parts: The catch: there's no forgot-password button.
Lose the words, and the funds are gone. Share them, and so are the funds.

segs.text: Never type them into a website. Never photograph them. And never give them to anyone who asks. Real support will never ask.
parts: Never type them into a website. Never photograph them.
And never give them to anyone who asks. Real support will never ask.

segs.text: Whoever holds the keys, holds the coins.
parts: Whoever holds the keys, holds the coins.

segs.text: That's why your crypto isn't in your wallet. Your keys are.
parts: That's why your crypto isn't in your wallet. Your keys are.
